reviewContext.note: Phase 3 round 3 (fresh-context, zero prior-round trust, zero Builder context). Re-verifies FIND-003 (edge_case_coverage, medium) and FIND-004 (implementation_correctness, low) from round 2, claimed fixed in ~/anicca commit a8c3dc4. Methodology note (disclosed for honesty): this review environment provided Read/Write/Edit/Grep/Glob only, with NO command-execution tool -- I could not personally invoke `node --test`. I therefore did NOT independently execute the test suite. Instead I performed maximal-rigor STATIC verification: read the full current production source for every affected file end-to-end, read the ACTUAL delivered test files' verbatim assertions (not descriptions of them), and cross-referenced literal runtime strings (e.g. the exact console.error template in spawn-orchestrator.mjs:729 against the exact printed line in evidence/sprint-2-find003-004-fix.log:192) to corroborate that the evidence log reflects a genuine run of THIS code, not a fabricated/stale one. This is a lower-confidence verification method than fresh execution and is flagged honestly rather than claimed as 'independently executed'.

evidence.location: specs/behavioral-spec.md lines 2559-2571 (REQ-305 Edge Case text) and lines 2848-2858 (REQ-307 Edge Case text, corrected contract-review round 13/FIND-020)
evidence.description: Re-read REQ-305's own transient-vs-permanent registry-append-failure edge case text and REQ-307's step-9 carve-out text in full. Confirmed the CURRENT spec text (not a prior, superseded version) explicitly names 'pending-registry-append.js' as the retry mechanism and explicitly distinguishes the transient-filesystem-error case (retry on next wake, ledger stays 'active') from the isSelfFunded-refusal case (permanently excluded, requires explicit remediation, never blindly retried) -- and the delivered code in spawn-orchestrator.mjs genuinely implements exactly this distinction: the isSelfFunded() check (line 709) gates BEFORE the try/catch even runs (a refused record is never queued to pending-registry-append.js at all, it only logs and moves on), while the try/catch (lines 710-731) is scoped ONLY to the appendCitizenRecord call itself, so only a genuine filesystem-layer throw (ENOTDIR/EACCES/ENOSPC-class) is caught and queued. No conflation of the two failure modes exists in the delivered code.

evidence.location: contracts/sprint-2.md lines 272-311 (the FIND-003/FIND-004 correction paragraph) vs. actual delivered files
evidence.description: Cross-checked every specific file-touch claim in the contract's own correction paragraph against the actual filesystem: pending-registry-append.js genuinely exists and genuinely exports {readPendingRegistryAppends, queuePendingRegistryAppend, resolvePendingRegistryAppend, deriveOutstandingRegistryAppends} exactly as claimed; wake-gate.mjs genuinely gained a retryPendingRegistryAppends call site (lines 143-146) gated on !dryRun, positioned before filterProductiveCitizens/decideColonySpawn (lines 151+/169+), exactly as claimed; gen-solana-wallet.test.mjs genuinely now imports @solana/web3.js's Keypair.fromSecretKey via require('@solana/web3.js') (line 78) rather than a second solana-keygen shell-out. All claims verified true against the actual current source, not merely accepted from the contract's own prose.

FIND-003 CONFIRMED-FIXED by direct read. The appendCitizenRecord(citizensRegistryFile, citizenRecord) call (line 711) IS now wrapped in try/catch (lines 710-731). On a caught error: (a) executeSpawnAttempt does NOT rethrow/reject -- control falls through to `return { status: 'active', childId }` at line 738, so the function's own documented return-type contract (JSDoc line 476, Promise<{status:'active'|'failed', childId, error?}>) is honored, never a rejection; (b) the ledger 'active' row (line 698) was already written moments earlier and is untouched by the later registry-append failure -- confirmed the ledger write and the registry-append are two textually and temporally separate statements, the first never conditioned on the second's success; (c) queuePendingRegistryAppend(pendingFile, {...}) (lines 721-727) durably records childId, the full citizenRecord, the target citizensRegistryFile, queuedMs, and the real error message -- this record lives in pending-registry-append.js (a genuinely new module, read in full: reuses ledger.js's generic (file,row) JSONL primitives, last-row-wins-per-child_id semantics for deriveOutstandingRegistryAppends, matching children.jsonl's own established convention).

Confirmed the 'retry on next wake, before any further spawn evaluation runs' requirement is genuinely satisfied by call-site ordering, not merely by the retry function's own existence: runWakeGate's non-dry-run branch calls `await retryPendingRegistryAppends({ pendingRegistryAppendsFile: deps.pendingRegistryAppendsFile })` at line 145, BEFORE `filterProductiveCitizens` (line 151), BEFORE `computeColonySurplusUsd` (line 159), and BEFORE `decideColonySpawn` (line 170) -- i.e. before any of REQ-102's own spawn-evaluation machinery runs on this wake. Correctly skipped when --dry-run is set (line 143 `if (!dryRun)`), matching dry-run's own pre-established zero-side-effect contract (a registry append is a real filesystem write). wake-gate.test.mjs's own real test ('FIND-003: a real (non-dry-run) wake calls retryPendingRegistryAppends BEFORE decideColonySpawn's own evaluation runs', lines 216-228) asserts call ORDER via a shared `calls` array (['retry','evaluate']), not merely that both were called -- this is a genuine ordering proof, read verbatim, not a description of one.

Read the two actual delivered FIND-003 tests verbatim (not a summary). Both genuinely reproduce the documented ENOTDIR scenario (citizensRegistryFile's parent segment is a plain file via `fs.writeFileSync(blockerFile, 'x')`, then `citizensRegistryFile: path.join(blockerFile, 'citizens.json')`) and assert: result.status==='active' (never a rejection -- if it rejected, the `await executeSpawnAttempt(...)` at line 328 would itself throw and fail the test with an uncaught exception, not merely a wrong assertion value), the ledger row is honestly 'active', citizens.json is genuinely empty (the transient failure genuinely did not silently succeed), and a durable pending row with status:'pending' and the real ENOTDIR error message exists. The second test then clears the blocker and calls the real (non-mocked) `retryPendingRegistryAppends`, confirming the SAME child_id is retried exactly once, the citizens.json append then genuinely lands, and a second retry call is correctly a no-op (no duplicate append) -- directly exercising deriveOutstandingRegistryAppends' last-row-wins/resolved-entry-exclusion logic on a real execution path, not a fixture in isolation.

No solana-keygen invocation appears anywhere in this test file (grep-equivalent confirmed by full read: the ONLY solana-keygen reference left is inside gen-solana-wallet.sh itself, the generation side, never the check side).

Confirmed @solana/web3.js (^1.98.4) is a genuine, real top-level dependency declared in the repo's own package.json alongside bs58 and viem -- not merely referenced in a comment or a test-only devDependency, and not a phantom/aspirational import. This is the same library runtime/wallet-address-solana.mjs already uses (per the test's own comment, independently plausible given viem's already-confirmed real EVM equivalent usage elsewhere in this codebase).

Re-confirmed no money-safety regression alongside the FIND-003 fix: defaultReclaimSeed/attemptSeedReclaim (lines 390-436, FIND-001's fix) are byte-for-byte the same reclaim logic verified in round 2 -- the FIND-003 diff touches ONLY step 9 (lines 695-736) and adds the new retryPendingRegistryAppends export (lines 760-775); it does not touch seedUsdcAmount, defaultDeploy's funding-gate wiring, or any spend-cap/reclaim code path. defaultDeploy (lines 267-301) still gates every Akash deploy behind evaluateAkashFundingGate's two-pass check before any spend, unchanged from round 2. No `external:true` flag appears anywhere in this diff's scope.

CRIT-201/CRIT-202 re-confirmed unaffected: still exactly one executeSpawnAttempt entry point; the new retryPendingRegistryAppends is a genuinely separate, clearly-named function (not a second orchestration path competing with executeSpawnAttempt -- it never re-runs steps 1-9, only completes the one queued sub-operation). pending-registry-append.js is a small (45-line), single-purpose module reusing ledger.js's existing generic primitives -- no duplication of read/append logic, matching this codebase's own established 'reuse, never reimplement' convention (already used identically by shelter-cost-ledger.js).
